newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel declines on fraud scandal.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel declines on fraud scandal.

text.p: The shekel's representative rate was fixed lower against the dollar and currency basket on Thursday in volatile, nervous trading in the wake of a scandal threatening to topple the Israeli government, dealers said.
"The session opened with aggressive buying of foreign currency. Investors panicked because of the political situation and started running to the dollar," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi.
Police said on Wednesday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should be charged with fraud and breach of trust in an influence-peddling scandal.
Netanyahu refused to quit, but legal experts say a decision to charge the prime minister would force him to resign and prompt new elections.
"Whan the dollar reached 3.4210 shekels other investors used the opportunity and started taking profits and the shekel recovered," Sadeh said.
He added that later in the day the market was stable and activity declined.
"Investors are waiting for further developments. If Netanyahu resigns the market might fall again," he said.

Traders noted that the local market was paying no attention on Thursday to changes in world forex markets. "At the beginning of the day the dollar rose here despite the fact that it declined abroad. Later, the dollar rose overseas and declined in the local market," Sadeh said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4040 shekels against 3.3980 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6772 shekels against 3.6705 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7071 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7005 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9706 shekels after 1.9704 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4040 shekels.
